changelog.summary: Initial seed from manual analysis: 5-state transition matrix, Israel/Iran/China actor dynamics, live Fed/AI-capex/post-midterm variables.

First automated daily update, hours after the seed. Material 24-48h moves: Brent +~7% to ~$90 on the Jul 29 reescalation (Forbes/Fortune/oilprice); the July 28-29 FOMC resolved as a hawkish hold (rates unchanged, 3 dissents favoring a hike) with the 10-year rising ~5bp to ~4.66% and equities selling off (CNBC). Refreshed ai_capex_credit with late-July hyperscaler earnings/credit signals (FactSet, UBS via reporting). Left SPR at 307.7M: the newest named EIA weekly figure (311.4M, week of Jul 17) predates the seed's basis, so there is no fresher release to update from. Held current_state_estimate at II, the transition_matrix, and all actor profiles unchanged: the dual-chokepoint (Hormuz + Bab al-Mandeb) closure was already reflected in the seed and no new war-cycle transition or actor-specific domestic development occurred in the last 24-48h.

Moved current_state_estimate II->III (Dual Chokepoint Escalation). The Jul 29 reescalation widened rather than paused over the last 48h: Strait of Hormuz still closed and Bab al-Mandeb under the Houthis' Jul 20 maritime embargo (traffic down ~56% per The National/USNI) = confirmed dual-chokepoint disruption; regional spillover with Egypt struck for the first time Jul 30 (CNN), US-Saudi joint strikes on Iranian proxies in Iraq (CBS/NBC), and a Saudi-led ~13-nation Red Sea protection coalition (HQ Riyadh; UAE/Oman declined) announced Jul 30 (Al Jazeera). Trump said Jul 31 he is 'losing faith' with Iran but has not ruled out a deal; Iran says it has no direct US talks, only Oman channel on Hormuz (ABC/Al Jazeera). Economic_snapshot: Brent to ~$92 (Fortune, $92.27 Jul 31, ~flat day-on-day); 10-year 4.67% (Trading Economics, Jul 31, ~flat). SPR left at 307.7M (stale; no fresher EIA weekly figure found). Transition_matrix, war_cycle_history, and all four actor profiles held unchanged: the widening is war-conduct news, not a new cycle transition (no ceasefire/pause) or an actor-specific domestic development, and no new Taiwan/China/Israel/US-domestic news surfaced.

taiwan_strait.label: Taiwan Strait Tension
taiwan_strait.detail: China ran two-day live-fire drills in the western Taiwan Strait July 23-24 alongside wider coastguard 'squeeze' patrols around the island, and held Joint Sea-2026 naval exercises with Russia July 6-13. The drills came a day after July 22 Rubio-Wang Yi talks and were condemned by Taipei as a 'gray-zone' provocation. Taiwan's Lai has called for a $40B defense-spending increase, currently stalled in the legislature. Not yet linked to the Iran-war transition matrix as a numeric input; tracked here as an independent watch item per the polycrisis discussion.

fed_decision.label: FOMC Decision
fed_decision.detail: Warsh's Fed held rates unchanged at the July 28-29 meeting, with three members dissenting in favor of a hike and the Committee preserving the option to tighten further if inflation proves persistent. The 10-year yield rose ~5bp to ~4.66% and equities sold off (Dow -1.6%) on the announcement.

ai_capex_credit.label: AI Capex / Private Credit Stress
ai_capex_credit.detail: AI capex ~93% of hyperscaler operating cash flow (was 33% in 2023). $3.3T semiconductor selloff July 21. BIS flagged AI/private-credit as a top-4 systemic risk in its 2026 Annual Report. Late-July earnings sharpened the credit angle: Alphabet guided 2026 capex to $195-205B (shares -7% on the week) and Meta to $125-145B; FactSet notes hyperscaler debt-funded capex rose from 9% of capex (FY24) to 32% LTM, and UBS cut its leveraged-loan forecast on the view that AI-disruption risk is underpriced in loan and private-credit markets.

post_midterm_restraint.label: Post-Midterm De-Restraint
post_midterm_restraint.detail: Activates after Nov 3, 2026 if Republicans lose the House as projected (217-214 margin). Commentary already frames Iran posture as lame-duck legacy-seeking.

current_state_estimate.rationale: Moved II->III: the Jul 29 reescalation has widened rather than paused, with the Strait of Hormuz still closed and Bab al-Mandeb under the Houthis' Jul 20 embargo (dual-chokepoint disruption), plus regional spillover (Egypt struck for the first time Jul 30 per CNN, US-Saudi joint strikes on Iranian proxies in Iraq, and a Saudi-led ~13-nation Red Sea coalition announced Jul 30 per Al Jazeera) that fits 'Dual Chokepoint Escalation' rather than a grinding status quo.

israel.name: Israel
israel.subtitle: Netanyahu — Fall 2026 Election
israel.core_incentive: Facing a fall election Netanyahu is projected to struggle to win; only 15% of Israelis believe the Iran war produced a clear victory, and the 'rally around the flag' bump is fading.
israel.key_constraint: Coalition dependency on right-wing/ultra-Orthodox partners favoring hardline posture, against a visibly cooling Trump relationship and diverging war aims.
modifiers: II→III raised: independent electoral incentive toward renewed confrontation.
I persistence lowered: durable ceasefire removes Netanyahu's most reliable unifying narrative.
Raises risk of Israeli unilateral action decoupled from Washington's posture.

iran.name: Iran
iran.subtitle: Mojtaba Khamenei — ‘Phantom’ Supreme Leader
iran.core_incentive: Installed under IRGC pressure after his father's Feb 28 assassination; zero verified public appearances since. Authority borrowed entirely from the security apparatus.
iran.key_constraint: No arbiter left to contain factional rivalries; individual strikes may reflect factional signaling rather than centralized strategy. Deep socio-economic crisis (inflation, water, unemployment) running in parallel.
modifiers: Raises volatility across all cells — surprise transitions more likely than a unitary-actor model predicts.
I stability lowered: fragmented command may be unable to enforce a durable ceasefire on all factions.
Economic collapse could eventually push toward negotiated exit, in tension with hardliner legitimacy needs.

china.name: China
china.subtitle: Wang Yi — ‘Friend to All’ Positioning
china.core_incentive: Revealed preference is de-escalation: 40%+ of crude imports originate from the Middle East. Overriding priority is protecting the Trump-Xi relationship.
china.key_constraint: Real but limited mediation leverage — Pakistan, not China, brokered the April ceasefire. Still supplies Iran dual-use tech and vetoed a Bahrain-led UNSC resolution alongside Russia.
modifiers: III→II reversion raised: genuine incentive to discourage chokepoint escalation raising its own import costs.
Petroyuan/systemic trend continues regardless — banked passively, not accelerated deliberately.
Moderating influence may be maximized around summit windows and recede afterward.

us.name: United States
us.subtitle: Trump Administration — War Unpopularity vs. Legacy Incentive
us.core_incentive: The war remains historically unpopular domestically, but a decisive resolution (or a dramatic escalation framed as forcing one) offers a legacy narrative Trump has shown clear interest in. After Nov 3, 2026, a probable loss of the House removes most domestic legislative options, raising the relative weight of unilateral foreign-policy action as his primary remaining lever.
us.key_constraint: A Democratic-controlled House could raise War Powers Resolution and appropriations challenges, a countervailing force to reduced electoral restraint. Pentagon/CENTCOM readiness is separately strained by Patriot interceptor demand shared across the Iran, Israel, and Ukraine theaters simultaneously.
modifiers: II→IV raised after Nov 3: reduced legislative restraint increases the odds of unilateral escalatory moves.
I persistence uncertain: a durable resolution could itself serve as the legacy achievement, competing with an escalatory legacy narrative rather than clearly favoring one.
War Powers pushback could offset lame-duck freedom — net effect on volatility more clearly predictable than net effect on direction.
